**[P2] Exercise scratch-backed K rows in the staging test**

The new K callback can return the supplied scratch buffer. `gof::populate` collects every head pointer before `k.set_position` copies their values. Each head therefore needs a distinct scratch row until that copy finishes. [Implementation](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/blob/a711aeee831c7c4da24ce3737d93dd0c76df1149/src/tron/gof.cpp#L203-L219).

This callback ignores scratch, as do the other changed K test callbacks. This case checks only `g.populated`; the concurrent case checks V values only. Removing `h * HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE` from the new K scratch address would leave those checks unchanged, while scratch-backed callbacks would stage the last head's data for every head. This is missing coverage of the new buffer contract; the current stride is correct.

Please extend this existing fake-device case to gather distinct packed K data for at least two heads into the supplied scratch and return it. After `populate`, unshuffle and compare K values for all four tokens, heads and dimensions. Removing the head stride should then fail. This can run without FPGA hardware.

**[P2] Keep the previous limits for the unchanged row-major path**

This raises the absolute error limit for the weighted V sum from 0.02 to 0.05 even with `TRON_K_VNNI=OFF`. The same change appears at line 2872. The option-off implementation retains its original row-major reader, and the description reports that it passes the previous bounds. A 0.03-unit discrepancy would now pass where the previous test rejected it. The third argument is an absolute limit. [Helper](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/blob/a711aeee831c7c4da24ce3737d93dd0c76df1149/t/testutil.hpp#L52-L68).

Please select the wider limit only for the packed layout that needs it, preserving the existing assertions for row-major storage. The weight-sum assertion at line 2733 also changes from an absolute to a relative limit for both layouts; keep its previous option-off check unless there is separate evidence that it needs to change. This concern is the loss of existing coverage, not the documented need for a different packed-layout tolerance.

**[P3] Limit the poison-test claim to what its assertions observe**

An unmasked K load would put the inactive tokens' NaNs in inactive vector lanes. The reader never combines token lanes, and its final masked store discards those lanes. Thus replacing the masked load at `kernels/k_vnni.hpp:97` with an unmasked load would not, by itself, change the scores checked here. [Load and store](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/blob/a711aeee831c7c4da24ce3737d93dd0c76df1149/h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp#L94-L123).

The implementation does use a masked load. The issue is the test's claim of detecting a stray read. Please describe the observed contract instead:

```suggestion
  // preset value. Their storage holds NaN (not a number) poison.
  // Check that dead-token values cannot affect live scores.
```

Likewise, line 232 can say `Dead-token score slots must retain this preset.` Proving that no read occurs would require a different check. This conclusion follows from the lane operations; I did not run the mutation.

**Optional — Ben pass: reuse the K destination-row helper**

This temporary is a contiguous K transfer row, the concept already named by `k_destination_row`. Reusing that helper makes the row's role explicit and keeps the element type, alignment flag and shape in one definition. It produces the same view type here. [Helper](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/blob/a711aeee831c7c4da24ce3737d93dd0c76df1149/h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp#L224-L252).

```suggestion
              k_destination_row<geometry.kv.head_size>(row).set(kout);
```

Keep `k_source_row(kout)` in the bf16 branch: that overload preserves the source buffer's own flags.

review:
**Short version:** I found two test-coverage issues, an inaccurate test comment, and two description claims to narrow. No reachable production correctness defect was established. The inline comments distinguish coverage requests from the optional readability suggestion.

Reviewed commit `a711aeee831c7c4da24ce3737d93dd0c76df1149` against `72308ec90c80318403c4575dd9ce4a3bc9af5033`.

K and V mean the saved key and value vectors used by attention. The packed layout stores K in dimension pairs. `TRON_K_VNNI` selects that layout for heads with 128 dimensions. FPGA means the programmable hardware accelerator; AMX is the CPU matrix instruction set; bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format.

The default review finished before the separate skill passes:

| Pass | Result |
|---|---|
| Default review | Production storage, reader, staging, build settings and tests traced. Two coverage issues and claim corrections identified. |
| Ben | One optional reuse of the existing K destination-row helper. |
| Tron | Confirmed the staging-test gap and broader-than-needed tolerance change. Traced buffer ownership, completion and statistics. |
| Wade | All 35 numbered checks assessed, including both parts of check 3. Results and limits below. |
| Positron | No temporary review-round or reviewer-specific narration found. |
| Plain English | Description checked separately. Exact phrases, fixes and the complete suggested text are in the accompanying comments. |

**Description accuracy**

- The “CI coverage” paragraph says the packed branches of all three named binaries do not execute in required continuous integration (CI), and those binaries run row-major paths. The first three `t_k_vnni_layout` cases directly exercise packed storage and the reader regardless of `TRON_K_VNNI`. Only its cache-integration case selects the layout with that option. With `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF`, `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` runs a success placeholder. It does not test row-major attention. Please distinguish those cases from the option-on cache/model path that required CI currently misses. The accepted exception and follow-up [#4865](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4865) remain applicable. [Packed tests](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/blob/a711aeee831c7c4da24ce3737d93dd0c76df1149/t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp#L101-L349), [dispatch-off case](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/blob/a711aeee831c7c4da24ce3737d93dd0c76df1149/t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp#L293-L296).
- “The next PR of the stack ... removes the gate and the loss” promises an unmeasured performance result. Gate removal is a planned code change. Recovery of the measured performance loss needs measurements at that next PR’s final commit. Please label recovery as expected until those measurements exist.

**Evidence and limits**

- Source inspection covered the full change and relevant callers, including synchronous copying of the new scratch rows into owned staging buffers. No scratch pointer is submitted for an asynchronous device transfer.
- Independent arithmetic checks covered all 8,192 packed coordinates and query-group splits. Recalculation of the saved performance measurements agreed with their summaries. These checks do not replace compiled tests.
- I inspected the author’s saved validation evidence. I did not rerun the compiled suite, sanitizers or hardware workloads. The recorded host suite has 93 passing tests, one skipped test and one failed test; the description identifies the missing Python environment exception. I am not reporting that suite as entirely passing.
- Required CI at this snapshot has eight passing checks. [Build Tron](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/actions/runs/38061977018/job/114243529022) is still running. **Insufficient data** for a completed required-CI verdict; that job and any downstream checks must finish.
- Wade’s checks used full-file scans, changed-function reads and caller tracing. I did not read every unchanged line of the large existing files. The optional dictionary-based spelling checker was unavailable; prose and identifier checks were performed without it.
- The existing [Cursor bounds-check comment](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/4868#discussion_r4238076829) was traced to current callers. The low-level helpers lack their own token bound checks, but the production page accessors and copy entry point check their ranges. I found no reachable out-of-range production call and have not duplicated that thread.
- The two test comments ask for observed behavior. The staging suggestion extends an existing fake-device case, consistent with the repository’s instruction to “prefer extending the closest existing test.” [Test policy](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/blob/a711aeee831c7c4da24ce3737d93dd0c76df1149/AGENTS.md#L30-L56).

The documented add-order differences, temporary exclusion of the existing AMX kernel for packed slots, and accepted CI exception are not additional findings.
